title: Why does product search sometimes pause?
label: A SHOPPER WAITS FOR RESULTS
voice: A shopper searches for running shoes. Results arrive late. Is the database slow, or is our Java service struggling with memory? Measure before guessing.
note: A slow search is a symptom. Identify the bottleneck.

title: Search creates short-lived objects
label: HEAP AND REACHABILITY
voice: Search builds temporary product summaries. Many become unreachable after a response. Garbage collection reclaims them. Useful objects, such as a live catalogue cache, must remain.
note: Reachable is not the same as young. Age alone does not make garbage.

title: 2,000 ms search. 300 ms pause.
label: COMPARE SAME-SERVER EVIDENCE
voice: A two second search with a three hundred millisecond pause is not entirely a garbage collection problem. Compare database and inventory waits on the same timeline.
note: Illustrative intervals, not a measured performance result.

title: Profile before changing the collector
label: REMOVE PROVEN REDUNDANT WORK
voice: Use Java Flight Recorder to find allocation hotspots. Remove repeated serialization and bound caches. Preserve correct product prices and availability, then repeat the same workload.
note: Do not change business results to reduce allocations.

title: Java 21 adds Generational ZGC
label: YOUNG AND OLD GENERATIONS
voice: Java twenty one adds Generational ZGC. It collects young objects separately from longer lived objects. This can reduce allocation stalls compared with non generational ZGC.
note: G1 also has generations. This feature extends ZGC.

title: Test the benefit. Keep correct results.
label: VALIDATE THE WHOLE SEARCH SERVICE
voice: Most ZGC work runs concurrently. Compare tail latency, errors, CPU, and memory before choosing it. This lesson teaches the method; it does not claim a measured speedup.
note: Less GC overhead is useful only if the full workload improves.
